chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him the Peace about a house that had not yet been partitioned, so some of the people of the house gave charity with their share of the house. He said: 'It is valid.' I said: 'What do you think if it was a gift?' He said: 'It is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to give charity or gift a share of an undivided property in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that an owner of a fractional share in undivided common property (*musha*) retains the right to dispose of their specific portion through charity (*sadaqah*) or gift (*hibah*) without requiring the consent of other co-owners. This ruling underscores the principle that ownership of a share is distinct from physical possession of a specific part, allowing for independent legal transactions regarding one's equity in the joint asset.
